notes:
Summary: Evaluating Redwood Dedicated for latency-sensitive trading assistant and reranking for real-time risk decisions. Primary ask: hard throughput guarantees and traffic shaping primitives to ensure low-latency SLAs during market spikes.

Key constraints / quotes: "We need predictable p99 during market opens — spikes kill the model." — Head of Platform. Budget requires reserved GPU planning (quarterly commit).

Technical requirements (customer provided):
- Typical short-response calls: median length 40 tokens; target p50 < 30ms, p95 < 150ms, p99 < 300ms for single-turn chat on a 2B-7B family model variant.
- Heavy reranking jobs: batch throughput target 18k documents/sec sustained during end-of-day windows.
- Concurrency: up to 600 concurrent sessions in peak tranche; burst to 1.2k for <10m windows.
- Reserved capacity ask: baseline estimate 8x A100-equivalent GPUs reserved, ability to burst to additional shared pool.

Traffic shaping & priority lanes requirements discussed:
- Tenant isolation: want dedicated tenant pools for core trading stack; ability to tag routes as "high-priority" or "background".
- Per-route quotas: strict token/sec and concurrency caps per route with quota enforcement and graceful backpressure.
- Noisy-neighbor controls: preemption of best-effort lanes, soft isolation (cgroups / GPU slice limits), auto-throttling, and targeted shedding of lower-priority models during saturation.
- Priority lanes: guaranteed fast-path for critical routes (low-latency, pinned KV cache), and separate admission control for batch/rerank jobs.
- Fallbacks: automatic downgrade to smaller model variant or queued execution with SLA-credit triggers if p99 bound breached.

POC plan (agreed): 6-week evaluation. steps:
1) Week 0-1: finalize SLA language (p50/p95/p99 definitions and measurement hooks), exchange traffic profile traces.
2) Week 2: deploy Dedicated tenant pool in staging; configure priority lanes and per-route quotas.
3) Week 3: synthetic load + market-spike replay tests (we will provide trace). measure latency and tail behavior.
4) Week 4: run mixed workload stress test (chat + rerank + embeddings) and validate noisy-neighbor mitigations.
5) Week 5: run soak test and cost modeling with Redwood Optimize recommendations.
6) Week 6: acceptance review + exec summary; SLA draft for procurement.

Acceptance criteria (POC):
- p99 < 350ms for critical route under 95th percentile spike profile.
- Batch rerank throughput within 10% of target on reserved capacity.
- Per-route quotas enforceable and observable in Console (token-level breakdown).
- Noisy-neighbor scenario results in degradation of background lanes only.

SLA asks / negotiation points:
- Credits for p99 misses beyond agreed thresholds; clear measurement windows and telemetry ownership.
- Minimum reserved capacity must be able to burst to shared pool X times/month without additional commit cost — customer pushing for defined burst budget.
- Clarify circuit-breaker behavior and opt-in automatic fallback to hosted models in cross-region failover.
